chief_complaint: progressive breathlessness walking on flat ground and persistent dry Velcro cough for 1 year
hpi_details: 1-year history of insidious, slowly progressive shortness of breath on exertion, initially noticed when climbing hills but now breathless walking 100 metres on level ground or doing light housework. Accompanied by a persistent, irritating, dry, non-productive cough that is unaffected by bronchodilator inhalers, antihistamines, or antibiotics prescribed over the past 8 months. Reports chronic fatigue and unintentional 3kg weight loss over 6 months. Denies fever, night sweats, haemoptysis, chest pain, joint swelling, or skin rashes. Has lived in the same suburban home for 25 years with no birds, hot tubs, or occupational dust exposure. Never smoked cigarettes.
ideas: thinks her lungs are prematurely hardening or turning to scar tissue after multiple chest infections
concerns: terrified she has an untreatable terminal lung scarring disease that will suffocate her completely within a few years
expectations: wants specialized high-resolution CT lung scans and anti-fibrotic medication to stop the scarring from spreading
pmh: gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD - chronic heartburn for 10 years), mild osteoarthritis of knees
social_hx: never smoked, zero alcohol, retired primary school principal, lives with husband

clinical_knowledge.topic: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF - Usual Interstitial Pneumonia / UIP pattern on HRCT) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF - Usual Interstitial Pneumonia / UIP pattern on HRCT) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Review case in multidisciplinary Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) board (pulmonologists, thoracic radiologists, ILD pathologists), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: progressive breathlessness walking on flat ground and persistent dry Velcro cough for 1 year

Key HPI features: 1-year history of insidious, slowly progressive shortness of breath on exertion, initially noticed when climbing hills but now breathless walking 100 metres on level ground or doing light housework. Accompanied by a persistent, irritating, dry, non-productive cough that is unaffected by bronchodilator inhalers, antihistamines, or antibiotics prescribed over the past 8 months. Reports chronic fatigue and unintentional 3kg weight loss over 6 months. Denies fever, night sweats, haemoptysis, chest pain, joint swelling, or skin rashes. Has lived in the same suburban home for 25 years with no birds, hot tubs, or occupational dust exposure. Never smoked cigarettes.

Objective/Exam findings: Inspection: examine fingers demonstrating marked bilateral finger clubbing (present in >50% of IPF cases). Respiratory auscultation: listen to lung bases posteriorly -> classical, loud, bilateral, fine end-inspiratory 'Velcro-like' crackles best heard at the lung bases posteriorly (pathognomonic physical finding). Pulmonary Function Tests (PFTs / Spirometry): demonstrates classical Restrictive pattern with normal or elevated FEV1/FVC ratio (>0.80) combined with symmetrically reduced FVC and TLC. Check Diffusing Capacity for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO -> markedly reduced e.g., 45% predicted confirming impaired alveolar-capillary gas exchange). Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT): shows significant exertional oxygen desaturation (>4% drop below baseline). High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the Chest (non-contrast, thin-section 1mm slices): reveals definitive Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP) pattern -> bilateral, predominantly subpleural and basal reticular opacities, traction bronchiectasis, and pathognomonic honeycomb cysts with complete absence of ground-glass opacities or nodules. Autoimmune serology screen (ANA, RF, anti-CCP, ENA, anti-synthetase panel) completely negative (rules out connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease).
Relevant background/PMH: gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD - chronic heartburn for 10 years), mild osteoarthritis of knees
Current medications: omeprazole 20mg OD, paracetamol PRN
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF - Usual Interstitial Pneumonia / UIP pattern on HRCT).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Community-acquired pneumonia without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%).
management_principles: Review case in multidisciplinary Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) board (pulmonologists, thoracic radiologists, ILD pathologists)
Consider antifibrotic treatment only after ILD multidisciplinary confirmation, assessment of contraindications, and shared decision-making; monitor according to specialist protocol.
Avoid using immunosuppression for stable IPF unless a specialist identifies another indication or diagnosis.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 59F non-smoker presents with 1-year progressive exertional dyspnoea, refractory dry cough, and history of chronic GORD without occupational/environmental antigen exposure.
reference_soap.objective: Inspection: examine fingers demonstrating marked bilateral finger clubbing (present in >50% of IPF cases). Respiratory auscultation: listen to lung bases posteriorly -> classical, loud, bilateral, fine end-inspiratory 'Velcro-like' crackles best heard at the lung bases posteriorly (pathognomonic physical finding). Pulmonary Function Tests (PFTs / Spirometry): demonstrates classical Restrictive pattern with normal or elevated FEV1/FVC ratio (>0.80) combined with symmetrically reduced FVC and TLC. Check Diffusing Capacity for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO -> markedly reduced e.g., 45% predicted confirming impaired alveolar-capillary gas exchange). Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT): shows significant exertional oxygen desaturation (>4% drop below baseline). High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the Chest (non-contrast, thin-section 1mm slices): reveals definitive Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP) pattern -> bilateral, predominantly subpleural and basal reticular opacities, traction bronchiectasis, and pathognomonic honeycomb cysts with complete absence of ground-glass opacities or nodules. Autoimmune serology screen (ANA, RF, anti-CCP, ENA, anti-synthetase panel) completely negative (rules out connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease).
reference_soap.assessment: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF - Usual Interstitial Pneumonia / UIP pattern on HRCT). DDx: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis (differentiated by upper/mid zone predominance, ground-glass opacities, air trapping on expiratory CT, and positive bird/mold exposure), Rheumatoid Arthritis or Scleroderma associated ILD (check serology/joint signs), Asbestosis (check occupational history/pleural plaques), Sarcoidosis.
reference_soap.plan: Refer urgently to an ILD multidisciplinary team to confirm the diagnosis, exclude alternative causes, assess severity, and discuss specialist-directed treatment. Assess exertional and resting oxygenation; provide monitored oxygen only when hypoxemia is present and clinically indicated. Arrange pulmonary rehabilitation, symptom support, and follow-up as appropriate. Seek emergency care for new severe breathlessness, hypoxemia, chest pain, syncope, haemoptysis, or concern for PE or ACS.

learning_objectives: Identify the pathognomonic physical signs of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: fine basal end-inspiratory Velcro crackles and digital clubbing
Interpret PFTs showing restrictive deficit with severely impaired DLCO alongside HRCT subpleural/basal honeycombing (UIP pattern)
Explain why anti-fibrotic agents (pirfenidone/nintedanib) are indicated while immunosuppressive steroids/azathioprine are strictly harmful in IPF
Formulate multidisciplinary ILD management integrating ambulatory oxygen, pulmonary rehabilitation, and early transplant referral

teaching.one_liner: Pulmonology case presenting with progressive breathlessness walking on flat ground and persistent dry Velcro cough for 1 year.
differentials: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
Chronic heart failure with pulmonary congestion
red_flags: Massive hemoptysis, chest pain, syncope, or abrupt deterioration suggesting PE, ACS, or another emergency

must_ask.say: When did you first notice the breathlessness, and has it steadily worsened over the year, or come and go?

must_ask.objective: Dry cough characteristics and treatment response
must_ask.say: Is your cough dry, and has it responded at all to inhalers, allergy medicine, or antibiotics you've tried?
Have you ever worked around dust, asbestos, or birds, or used a hot tub, that might affect your lungs?

must_ask.objective: Clubbing and Velcro crackles on examination
must_ask.say: I'd like to look at your fingernails and listen carefully to the bottom of your lungs from behind.

must_ask.objective: Connective tissue disease and systemic symptom screen
must_ask.say: Have you had any joint pain or swelling, skin rashes, or Raynaud's-type color changes in your fingers?
